capacity_gib.description:
The storage capacity of the instance in gibibytes (GiB). Allowed values
are from '9000' to '7632000', depending on the 'perUnitStorageThroughput'.
See [Performance tiers and maximum storage
capacities](https://cloud.google.com/managed-lustre/docs/create-instance#performance-tiers)
for specific minimums, maximums, and step sizes for each performance tier.
capacity_gib.rationale: Provisioned storage capacity of the Lustre instance in GiB. This is a sizing/capacity choice and does not affect access, encryption, or exposure, so it is not a security policy target.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This just tells Terraform 'can you delete this or not' — it's a Terraform safety switch, not something that changes who can access the data.

description.description: A user-readable description of the instance.
description.rationale: Provides descriptive metadata for the resource.

filesystem.description:
The filesystem name for this instance. This name is used by client-side
tools, including when mounting the instance. Must be eight characters or
less and can only contain letters and numbers.
filesystem.rationale: The Lustre filesystem name/identifier for the instance. This is a naming choice with no security effect; we do not constrain resource names.

gke_support_enabled.description:
Indicates whether you want to enable support for GKE clients. By default,
GKE clients are not supported.
gke_support_enabled.rationale: Enables GKE workloads to access the Lustre filesystem, increasing the potential access surface.

instance_id.description:
The name of the Managed Lustre instance.

* Must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens.
* Must start with a letter.
* Must be between 1-63 characters.
* Must end with a number or a letter.
instance_id.rationale: Provides a unique identifier for the Lustre instance.

kms_key.description:
The Cloud KMS key name to use for data encryption.
If not set, the instance will use Google-managed encryption keys.
If set, the instance will use customer-managed encryption keys.
The key must be in the same region as the instance.
The key format is:
projects/{project}/locations/{location}/keyRings/{key_ring}/cryptoKeys/{key}
kms_key.rationale: Specifies the encryption key used to protect data at rest.

labels.description:
Labels as key value pairs.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Provides metadata for resource organization and management.

location.description: Resource ID segment making up resource 'name'. It identifies the resource within its parent collection as described in https://google.aip.dev/122.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

network.description:
The full name of the VPC network to which the instance is connected.
Must be in the format
'projects/{project_id}/global/networks/{network_name}'.
network.rationale: Determines the VPC network used to connect the Lustre instance and affects network isolation.

per_unit_storage_throughput.description:
The throughput of the instance in MBps per TiB. Valid values are 125, 250,
500, 1000.
See [Performance tiers and maximum storage
capacities](https://cloud.google.com/managed-lustre/docs/create-instance#performance-tiers)
for more information.

If the instance is using the Dynamic tier, this field must not be set or
must be set to zero.
per_unit_storage_throughput.rationale: Defines the storage performance level of the instance.

placement_policy.description:
The placement policy name for the instance in the format of
projects/{project}/locations/{location}/resourcePolicies/{resource_policy}
placement_policy.rationale: Controls resource placement for infrastructure and availability purposes.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Specifies the Google Cloud project in which the resource is created.

access_rules_options.description:
IP-based access rules for the Managed Lustre instance. These options
define the root user squash configuration.

access_rules_options.default_squash_gid.description:
The user squash GID for the default access rule.
This user squash GID applies to all root users connecting from clients
that are not matched by any of the access rules. If not set, the default
is 0 (no GID squash).
access_rules_options.default_squash_gid.rationale: Defines the GID mapping applied when root-user squashing is used.

access_rules_options.default_squash_mode.description:
The squash mode for the default access rule.
Possible values:
NO_SQUASH
ROOT_SQUASH
access_rules_options.default_squash_mode.rationale: Controls whether root privileges are retained or restricted for unmatched clients.

access_rules_options.default_squash_uid.description:
The user squash UID for the default access rule.
This user squash UID applies to all root users connecting from clients
that are not matched by any of the access rules. If not set, the default
is 0 (no UID squash).
access_rules_options.default_squash_uid.rationale: Defines the UID mapping applied when root-user squashing is used.

access_rules_options.access_rules.description: The access rules for the instance.

access_rules_options.access_rules.ip_add.description:
The IP address ranges to which to apply this access rule. Accepts
non-overlapping CIDR ranges (e.g., '192.168.1.0/24') and IP addresses
(e.g., '192.168.1.0').
access_rules_options.access_rules.ip_add.rationale: Specifies application-specific IP ranges to which an access rule applies.

access_rules_options.access_rules.name.description:
The name of the access rule policy group.
Must be 16 characters or less and include only alphanumeric characters
or '_'.
access_rules_options.access_rules.name.rationale: Provides an identifier for the access-rule group.

access_rules_options.access_rules.squash.description:
Squash mode for the access rule.
Possible values:
NO_SQUASH
ROOT_SQUASH
access_rules_options.access_rules.squash.rationale: Controls root-user privilege handling for clients matching the access rule.

dynamic_tier_options.description: Dynamic tier options for a Managed Lustre instance.

dynamic_tier_options.mode.description:
The dynamic tier mode of the instance.
Possible values:
DISABLED
DEFAULT_CACHE
dynamic_tier_options.mode.rationale: Controls the operating mode of the Dynamic storage tier.

maintenance_policy.description: Defines a maintenance policy for a resource.

maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.description: The exclusion windows for the instance. Currently limited to 1 window.

Represents a whole or partial calendar date, such as a birthday. The time of
day and time zone are either specified elsewhere or are insignificant. The
date is relative to the Gregorian Calendar. This can represent one of the
following:

* A full date, with non-zero year, month, and day values.
* A month and day, with a zero year (for example, an anniversary).
* A year on its own, with a zero month and a zero day.
* A year and month, with a zero day (for example, a credit card expiration
date).

Related types:

* google.type.TimeOfDay
* google.type.DateTime
* google.protobuf.Timestamp

Day of a month. Must be from 1 to 31 and valid for the year and month, or 0
to specify a year by itself or a year and month where the day isn't
significant.
maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.rationale: Day component of the exclusion window's end date. A scheduling value with no security implication.

maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.description:
Month of a year. Must be from 1 to 12, or 0 to specify a year without a
month and day.
maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.rationale: Month component of the exclusion window's end date. Same reasoning as day.

maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.description:
Year of the date. Must be from 1 to 9999, or 0 to specify a date without
a year.
maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.rationale: Year component of the exclusion window's end date. Same reasoning as day.

Day of a month. Must be from 1 to 31 and valid for the year and month, or 0

maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.rationale: Day component of the exclusion window's start date. Scheduling only.

maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.description:
Month of a year. Must be from 1 to 12, or 0 to specify a year without a
month and day.
maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.rationale: Month component of the exclusion window's start date. Scheduling only.

maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.description:
Year of the date. Must be from 1 to 9999, or 0 to specify a date without

maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.rationale: Year component of the exclusion window's start date. Scheduling only.

maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.description:
Represents a time of day. The date and time zone are either not significant
or are specified elsewhere. An API may choose to allow leap seconds. Related
types are google.type.Date and 'google.protobuf.Timestamp'.

Hours of a day in 24 hour format. Must be greater than or equal to 0 and
typically must be less than or equal to 23. An API may choose to allow the
value "24:00:00" for scenarios like business closing time.
maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.rationale: Hour value within the exclusion window's time-of-day. No security relevance.

maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.description:
Minutes of an hour. Must be greater than or equal to 0 and less than or
equal to 59.
maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.rationale: Minute value within the exclusion window's time-of-day. No security relevance.

maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.description:
Fractions of seconds, in nanoseconds. Must be greater than or equal to 0
and less than or equal to 999,999,999.
maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.rationale: Sub-second precision for the exclusion window's time-of-day. No security relevance.

maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.description:
Seconds of a minute. Must be greater than or equal to 0 and typically must
be less than or equal to 59. An API may allow the value 60 if it allows
leap-seconds.
maintenance_policy.maintenance_exclusion.rationale: Second value within the exclusion window's time-of-day. No security relevance.

maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.description:
The weekly maintenance windows for the instance. Currently limited to 1
window.

Possible values:
MONDAY
TUESDAY
WEDNESDAY
THURSDAY
FRIDAY
SATURDAY
SUNDAY
maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.rationale: Day of the week on which the maintenance window occurs. Scheduling value only.
